hero.title: Marmo EDU
hero.subtitle: Award-Winning Educational Platform
hero.description: A comprehensive Flutter mobile and web application with full Python backend, connecting students to multiple educational data sources in one unified platform.

overview.title: Project Overview
overview.description: Marmo EDU is a full-featured educational platform that combines a polished Flutter application (mobile & web) with a robust Python backend. The app integrates with multiple data sources including Librus, Edupage, JakDojade, and WolneLektury to provide students with a unified hub for all their educational needs. Built with Docker for scalability and featuring fast, secure Google Sign-In for multiplatform availability and enhanced user experience.

hero.eyebrow: Built on Schooly · Part of Projekt Unity
hero.title: Spotty
hero.subtitle: One app for student life, for every school that joins.
hero.description: Spotty puts a student's whole school day in one place: timetable and substitutions, news, a QR student card for partner discounts, the school library, lunch and merch. It runs on Schooly, a white-label platform I designed so any school can launch its own instance without starting from scratch.
hero.role: Creator & lead developer · CTO of Projekt Unity

problem.title: Every school was solving the same problems alone.
problem.description: School life is spread across class chats, Instagram stories, a substitutions board, a library catalogue and posters on the corridor wall. Student councils in every school build their own fixes, and a good idea rarely travels to the next one. Spotty gives students one app, and Schooly lets the next school reuse everything the first one built.

points.title: One place
points.text: Timetable, substitutions, news, discounts, library, food and merch in a single app.

points.title: Run by students
points.text: Student councils publish content themselves through the Schooly CMS, with no developer in the loop.

points.title: Built to be shared
points.text: Each school is an instance of the same platform: its own content, branding and modules.

features.title: A whole school day in one app

items.title: Everything at a glance
items.text: The home screen greets you with today's lessons, the latest news and widgets for the things you use most. Students choose which sections appear and in what order.

items.title: Student card & partner perks
items.text: A QR student card lives in the wallet next to local partners: cafés, restaurants and shops that offer discounts. Partners can run loyalty programmes with stamps and rewards collected at the till.

items.title: Timetable & substitutions
items.text: Your own timetable with your groups and subjects, plus substitutions for your class pulled from the school's system. After your last lesson the view rolls over to tomorrow, and a push notification tells you when something changes.

items.title: The school library, searchable
items.text: The whole school library catalogue, searchable with typo tolerance, with live per-copy availability: on the shelf, borrowed, or read-on-site only. Borrowed books show up with their due dates.

items.title: Lunch & merch drops
items.text: The weekly catering menu, imported automatically from the caterer's flyers, and a merch shop that runs in drops with a countdown, sizes and order tracking until pickup.
bullets: Weekly menu read from flyers with OCR

items.title: An assistant that knows your school
items.text: Pull down for an AI assistant that answers questions from the school's own content and can check your substitutions. Notifications are opt-in per topic, so students only hear about what they care about.

unityId.title: Unity ID: one account for every Unity service
unityId.description: Projekt Unity is a network of student councils across Wrocław high schools. Unity ID is its shared account: students sign up once and use the same login in Spotty and in other Unity services, such as event tickets and the councils' shared workspace.

points.title: Passwordless
points.text: Students sign in with a passkey: fingerprint, face or phone PIN. Invite codes and one-time e-mail codes cover everyone else.

points.title: One identity
points.text: An OpenID Connect provider issues the identity, and every product keeps its own data linked to that single account.

points.title: Data shared only with consent
points.text: Another Unity product can read Spotty data, such as a timetable, only through Spotty's API with the student's explicit, revocable consent for a narrow scope.

platform.title: Schooly is the engine, Spotty is what students see
platform.description: Spotty is a white-label product. Students only ever see Spotty; underneath, everything is Schooly: one codebase, one backend and one CMS serving many schools.

schooly.subtitle: Platform

architecture.title: How it fits together
architecture.ops: Observability: Sentry crash reports, Umami analytics, Better Stack uptime monitors and heartbeats.

items.title: Substitutions, private by design
items.text: The school's substitutions board names teachers. The parser reads a name only long enough to classify a row and throws it away, so no name reaches the cache, the API or the AI assistant. One background watcher keeps the cache warm and exposes a health endpoint. Student requests that used to hang on 15-second timeouts are now served straight from the cache.

items.title: A library with no API
items.text: The city's library system has no public API, so a weekly crawler parses its HTML into Postgres, about 14k records with full-text and typo-tolerant search. Per-copy availability is fetched live and cached for 15 minutes, and a cover pipeline falls back through three sources to find book covers.

items.title: Feature flags that can't be bypassed
items.text: Flags resolve in SQL: a global default plus per-student overrides, read through a view under row-level security. Sensitive features are enforced on the server too, and beta programmes with caps and waitlists let me ship to testers without a store release.

items.title: A web app that feels native
items.text: The web build compiles to WebAssembly and installs as a PWA on iPhones. Trimming the bundled localisations cut the JavaScript by 10%, and a content cache keyed on CMS webhook revisions means the app only downloads what actually changed.
